title: GPU degradation radar brief — triage heuristics and runbook sketch
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact working brief meant for on-call SREs and infra engineers handling a rising class of GPU degradation incidents observed over Q3–Q4 2029. It synthesizes recurring signals we've seen (soft ECC bursts, inter-GPU fabric negotiation failures, transient driver restarts that precede kernel panics), proposes a minimal on-call triage heuristic, and sketches a lightweight runbook and instrumentation tasks that can be implemented quickly.
content_long:
Executive summary:
- Pattern: short-lived but repeating degradations on subsets of nodes where measurable soft ECC counts spike for a few minutes, followed by increased NVLink negotiation errors and, in a subset of cases, a driver module restart and then an OOPS/kernel panic within 1–6 minutes.
- Customer impact: degraded throughput (higher token-latency tails) and occasional RPC-level errors. Incidents are usually auto-healed by node restart but cause job evictions and QoS hits.
- Hypothesis: a combination of thermal-induced signal integrity issues across the NVLink retimer + a timing-sensitive driver path that mis-handles a corrected ECC burst, leading to a race during kernel module recovery.

Observed signals to check (quick checklist for first 10 minutes):
1) Cluster-wide: check alert flood — correlated CPU/system-disk alerts are usually absent. Focus on GPU telemetry.
2) Node-level: Query last 15m for correctable_ecc_count and uncorrectable_ecc_count. Example query (PromQL-ish):
   sum by (node) (increase(gpu_memory_correctable_errors_total[15m])) > 0
3) NVLink/Link errors: look for nvlink_negotiation_fail or link_down counters (we currently expose: nvlink_link_error_count, nvlink_retrain_count).
4) Driver churn: check kernel logs for "NVRM: Xid" messages, "nvidia: probe" or module reload events, and for backtraces referencing nv-kernel or nvlink.
   commands: journalctl -k --dmesg | grep -Ei "NVRM|nvlink|nvidia|oops|traceback"
5) Process symptoms: long tail latencies for inference worker (stacked GPU queue depth), repeated context loss messages in runtime logs.
6) Thermal & power: inspect GPU and board thermals (nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,temperature.memory,power.draw --format=csv) and BMC system logs for VRM watchdogs.

Immediate triage heuristic (fast path):
- If correctable ECC counts are isolated to a single GPU and driver is stable: move workloads off that GPU (pin away / taint GPU) and schedule a maintenance window for hardware inspection. Note: eviction without node reboot preserves more throughput.
- If ECC spikes + nvlink negotiation errors across multi-GPU pair(s) + driver churn: mark the node quarantined and initiate rolling-restart of the node (graceful drain -> reboot). Avoid live patching driver during active NVLink errors.
- If a full kernel panic occurred: capture crash dump (kdump if enabled), attach dmesg/journal, and follow postmortem template. Do not immediately repro on same kernel/driver pair; instead test on a staging node with instrumentation.

Runbook sketch (step-by-step for oncall):
1) Gather context (0–3m): node id, tenant jobs running, last driver version, kernel version, HW generation, cluster region. Attach to incident channel and tag owner.
2) Snapshot telemetry (3–6m): run provided helper: /opt/sre/bin/gpu-dump-quick --node $NODE --out /tmp/gpu-snapshot-$NODE.tar.gz (contains nvidia-smi -q, dmesg tail, nvlink counters, pmon snapshots).
3) Apply short-term mitigation (6–12m): if single-GPU correctable spike -> cordon GPU; if multi-GPU fabric errors -> cordon node and migrate critical workloads. Use runtime flag: redwoodctl node cordon $NODE --reason "nvlink-ecc-spike".
4) If driver showed module reloads or NVRM Xid codes: collect logs and escalate to firmware/driver oncall (tag: gpu-fw) with collected snapshot.
5) Execute safe cleanup (12–45m): graceful drain, reboot with clean kernel boot args (disable kdump auto-reboot if enabled), and observe for recurrence.
6) Post-restart observation (45–120m): keep node quarantined for at least 2 hours of normal traffic; run stress harness (see experiments below) if recurrence is suspected.

Severity classification guidance (quick):
- Sev3 (low): single-GPU correctable ECC spike; no driver churn; throughput impact <10% of jobs.
- Sev2 (medium): multi-GPU NVLink negotiation errors with transient driver restarts and measurable job evictions.
- Sev1 (high): kernel panic or repeated hard Xid failures causing persistent availability loss for customers.

Investigation heuristics and artifacts to collect:
- Crash logs: full journalctl -k, /var/log/kern.oops, dmesg before/after; kexec/kdump artefacts.
- NVLink firmware logs: where available, collect retimer counters and link status snapshots (we have a vendor helper: /opt/vendor/nvlink-inspector).
- Power/VRM telemetry: BMC sensor dumps covering VRM rails around the event timestamp.
- Model/query reproducibility: note any large-sequence or pinned workload patterns that were running (long context tokens, heavy KV cache usage) — these change traffic patterns and can increase memory pressure.

Short experiments for root-cause narrowing (non-blocking):
- Timing sensitivity test: on a single staging DGX, run synthetic load with memtest-like pattern + periodic nvlink re-train loops to try and provoke link negotiation under thermal load. Script: bench/nvlink-stress.sh (owner: eng-sre)
- Driver rollback & isolation: boot a staging node with previous driver (NVIDIA driver X.Y.Z-1) and run our standard inference harness for 2 hours to look for regression.
- Retimer firmware push test: small batch of nodes to vendor-signed firmware with increased margin; run A/B test for 48–72h.

Telemetry and short-term product suggestions (quick wins):
- Expose per-GPU cumulative correctable ECC counters in long-retention metrics (30d) and add a derived rate alert (10m sliding window) rather than absolute thresholds.
- Add nvlink negotiation-failure rate to our high-cardinality tracing events; correlate with node temperature and pcie link errors.
- Add a kprobe on the driver path that logs module reload reasons for 5% of reboots (sampled) to avoid high-volume logging.

Automations to reduce toil (P0/P1):
- Auto-quarantine rule: when (increase(correctable_ecc[5m]) > threshold) AND (nvlink_retrain_count_increase[5m] > 0) -> create quarantine tag and trigger graceful node drain. Keep a 30-minute cooldown window to reduce flapping.
- Smart-restart: if driver module reload is detected but no kernel OOPS reported in 10m, auto-limit tenant migrations (avoid noisy restarts).

Open questions / unresolved hypotheses:
- Are ECC bursts originating from memory subsystem (DIMM/board) or signal margin transients on retimers? Need vendor retimer traces to be sure.
- Does a specific job type (long-context chat sessions) correlate with higher probability? Need to instrument workload metadata at higher cardinality.
- Is there seasonal temperature correlation in particular racks/rooms (we saw more in racks fed by older PDUs)? correlate with datacenter change logs.

Next actions (owners and target dates):
- Short-term: add the incremental correctable-ECC 10m rate alert (owner: Mateo Alvarez) — target: 2029-11-01.
- Mid-term: implement auto-quarantine rule and 30m cooldown (owner: Priya Kapoor) — target: 2029-11-15.
- Investigation: schedule vendor firmware retimer trace session and push to 5 lab nodes (owner: Evan Chen) — request meeting with vendor by 2029-10-25.
- Postmortem: if a kernel panic occurred in this incident, open a postmortem ticket with the template in linked_artifacts (owner: oncall lead).

Useful commands snippet (copyable):
- Collect quick snapshot:
  sudo /opt/sre/bin/gpu-dump-quick --node $NODE --out /tmp/gpu-snapshot-$NODE.tar.gz
- Grep kernel logs for NV errors:
  sudo journalctl -k -u kubelet --since "15 minutes ago" | egrep -i "nvrm|nvlink|nvidia|xid|oops|panic" || true
- PromQL sample (alert idea):
  sum by (node) (increase(gpu_memory_correctable_errors_total[10m])) / sum by(node) (gpu_memory_total_bytes) > 1e-8

Incident notes (quick timeline example from recent signal):
- 2029-10-12 02:14 UTC: auto-alert fires: correctable ECC burst on node gpu-12c.
- 02:16: NVLink retrain increases across GPU0-GPU1. Driver logs show a probe/reload at 02:17. Jobs get evicted.
- 02:20: node quarantined and gracefully drained; rebooted 02:28. No kernel panic. Post-restart: correctable ECC counts persisted on same GPU -> SRE scheduled HW swap.

Appendix: short-form debugging checklist for oncall (one-line items):
- Capture snapshot: /opt/sre/bin/gpu-dump-quick
- Check ECC counters (Prometheus + nvidia-smi)
- Check nvlink retrain/negotiation counters
- Check for driver Xid messages in kernel logs
- If multi-GPU fabric involved -> cordon node
- If kernel panic -> capture crash dump and escalate

If anything in this brief is unclear or you hit a case that deviates from the heuristics above, add a note to the incident thread and ping eng-sre slack channel (#sre-gpu).

— Evan

Draft history: created 2029-10-17; edits 2029-10-19 (added automation suggestions and refined severity buckets).
